FLOW 3 — Journey Setup

```

├── Journey type (auto-filled from profile):

On tap CONFIRM:

STEP 1 — Call POST /risk/score

}

STEP 3 — Display to user:
──────────────────────────
├── Risk badge: 🔴 HIGH RISK
├── Risk factors listed
├── NEW — Signal warning if biker:

FLOW 4 — Active Journey

```
SCREEN: JourneyActive.jsx
─────────────────────────────────────────
Display:
├── Timer ring counting down
├── Risk level badge
├── "Running silently in background"
├── Map: current location + route
│       └── ⚠️ Signal markers on route  ← NEW
└── I'M SAFE button

BACKGROUND PROCESSES:
─────────────────────────────────────────

PROCESS A — GPS Polling (every 30 seconds)
──────────────────────────────────────────
Call POST /journey/ping
Request:
{
  journey_id: string,
  current_lat: float,
  current_lng: float,
  current_speed: float,
  timestamp: string
}

Response:
{
  status: "ok"|"deviation"|"stop"|"alert"|"signal_warning",
  message: string,
  signal_data: {           ← NEW — included if signal_warning
    name: string,
    distance_meters: int,
    incident_count: int
  }
}

Handle response:
├── "ok"             → continue silently
├── "deviation"      → show subtle warning banner
├── "stop"           → nudge: "Still okay? Tap to confirm"
├── "alert"          → trigger ALERT PIPELINE
└── "signal_warning" → trigger SIGNAL WARNING (see below)

─────────────────────────────────────────
NEW: SIGNAL WARNING SYSTEM
─────────────────────────────────────────

Triggered when: biker within 200m of high-risk signal

COMPONENT: SignalWarning.jsx
Display:
├── Phone vibrates (strong, 3 pulses)
├── Screen flashes briefly (even if locked)
└── Banner appears:
        ┌────────────────────────────────┐
        │ ⚠️ HIGH-RISK SIGNAL AHEAD      │
        │ Teen Talwar Signal — 180m      │
        │ 4 snatching reports this week  │
        │ Peak time: 9PM-12AM            │
        │                                │
        │ Keep phone hidden. Stay alert. │
        │              [OK]              │
        └────────────────────────────────┘

Rules:
├── Only shows if time matches peak hours
├── Only triggers once per signal per journey
├── Does NOT make sound (doesn't expose user)
└── Dismisses automatically after 8 seconds

─────────────────────────────────────────

PROCESS B — Shake Detection (continuous)
─────────────────────────────────────────
├── Listen to accelerometer
├── 3 shakes within 2 seconds
└── Call POST /alerts/trigger
    { trigger_type: "manual_sos" }

PROCESS C — Timer Countdown
────────────────────────────
├── Reaches 0 → Call POST /alerts/trigger
    { trigger_type: "timer_expired" }

USER TAPS "I'M SAFE":
──────────────────────
├── Call POST /journey/end
├── All processes stop
├── Zero alerts sent
└── Navigate → SafeArrival.jsx

FLOW 6 — Backend: Journey Ping + Signal Check

```
ENDPOINT: POST /journey/ping
─────────────────────────────────────────

STEP 1 — Route Anomaly (route_anomaly.py)
──────────────────────────────────────────
├── Shapely: distance from point to polyline
├── Beyond threshold → flag raised
└── 3 flags → return status: "alert"

STEP 2 — Stop Detection (stop_detector.py)
───────────────────────────────────────────
├── Speed < 2 km/h for threshold minutes?
├── Known traffic zone? → ignore
├── Near destination? → ignore
└── Unknown stop → return status: "stop"

STEP 3 — Signal Proximity Check (signal_risk.py) ← NEW
─────────────────────────────────────────────────
Only runs if journey_type == "biker"

├── Load signals_on_route (stored at journey start)
├── For each signal on route:
│       ├── Calculate distance from current GPS
│       │       to signal coordinates
│       ├── Distance < 200m?
│       │       └── YES → check if already warned
│       │               └── Not warned yet?
│       │                       └── return
│       │                           status: "signal_warning"
│       │                           signal_data: {
│       │                             name, distance,
│       │                             incident_count,
│       │                             peak_hours
│       │                           }
│       └── Mark signal as warned in Firebase
│               └── journeys/{id}/warned_signals: [id]
└── No signals within 200m → continue

STEP 4 — Update Firebase journey record
STEP 5 — Return response to mobile
```

FLOW 7 — Signal Risk Scoring (ML)

```
FILE: ml/signal_risk.py
─────────────────────────────────────────

DATA SOURCE: karachi_signals.geojson
─────────────────────────────────────────
Each signal record:
{
  signal_id: string,
  name: string,
  lat: float,
  lng: float,
  area: string,
  incident_history: [
    {
      type: "phone_snatching",
      datetime: "2024-11-15T22:30:00",
      reported_by: "user"|"cplc"
    }
  ]
}

SIGNAL RISK SCORE CALCULATION:
────────────────────────────────
For each signal, compute:

1. base_score:
        incidents_last_7_days × 0.4
        + incidents_last_30_days × 0.2
        + is_known_hotspot × 0.4

2. time_multiplier:
        └── Current hour in peak_hours?
                YES → × 1.5
                NO  → × 0.5

3. final_score = base_score × time_multiplier

RISK CLASSIFICATION:
        ≥ 0.7 → 🔴 HIGH
        0.4-0.7 → 🟡 MEDIUM
        < 0.4 → 🟢 LOW

ENDPOINT: GET /signals/map
└── Returns all signals with current risk scores

ENDPOINT: GET /signals/nearby?lat=&lng=
└── Returns signals within 2km
    sorted by risk score

ENDPOINT: POST /signals/on-route
Request: { polyline: [...] }
└── Returns all signals within
    300m of any polyline point
    Pre-loaded at journey start
```

FLOW 8 — Alert Pipeline

```
ENDPOINT: POST /alerts/trigger
─────────────────────────────────────────
Triggers:
├── ⏱️  Timer expired
├── 📍 Route deviation × 3
├── 🛑 Unusual stop unacknowledged
└── 📳 Shake × 3 manual SOS

STEP 1 — Fetch journey + user data
STEP 2 — Get real-time GPS
STEP 3 — Generate Google Maps link
        https://maps.google.com/?q={lat},{lng}

STEP 4 — Compose voice message:
        "[Name] was travelling and has not
         reached their destination. Their last
         known location is being sent to you now."

        Note: gender-neutral "their" —
        works for men and women

STEP 5 — Twilio Voice → Contact #1
        ├── Answered → stop escalation ✓
        └── No answer 30s → escalate

STEP 6 — Twilio Voice → Contact #2
        ├── Answered → stop ✓
        └── No answer → escalate

STEP 7 — Twilio Voice → Contact #3

STEP 8 — SMS → ALL 3 simultaneously:
        "[Name] may need help.
         Last known location:
         [Google Maps link]

         Do NOT call them back —
         it may escalate the situation.
         Go to location or contact
         authorities: 15 (Police)"

STEP 9 — Update Firebase:
        alerts/{alertId}:
            journeyId, trigger_type,
            lat, lng,
            contacts_notified,
            triggered_at
```

FLOW 9 — ML Risk Scorer

```
FILE: ml/risk_scorer.py
─────────────────────────────────────────
ENDPOINT: POST /risk/score

FEATURES:
├── hour_of_day: 0-23
│       Sine curve peaks at 23:00
├── day_of_week: 0-6
│       Fri/Sat night = highest weight
├── origin_crime_index: 0.0-1.0
│       Lookup karachi_crime.csv
├── destination_crime_index: 0.0-1.0
├── route_length_km: float
├── signals_on_route_count: int    ← NEW
│       More high-risk signals = higher score
├── high_risk_signals_count: int   ← NEW
│       Only RED signals counted
└── journey_type_weight:
        ride_hailing = 0.6
        solo = 0.8
        biker = 0.85               ← NEW
        (bikers most exposed to snatching)

MODEL:
└── RandomForestClassifier
    10,000 simulated journeys
    Output: 0.0 → 1.0 probability

RISK LEVELS:
├── 🟢 LOW (< 0.3)
│       deviation_threshold: 500m
│       stop_threshold: 7 min
│       signal_warning_distance: 200m
│
├── 🟡 MEDIUM (0.3-0.6)
│       deviation_threshold: 300m
│       stop_threshold: 5 min
│       signal_warning_distance: 250m
│       extra: halfway check-in
│
└── 🔴 HIGH (> 0.6)
        deviation_threshold: 200m
        stop_threshold: 3 min
        signal_warning_distance: 300m  ← warns earlier
        extra: contact pre-notified
```

FLOW 10 — Hotspot Clustering

```
FILE: ml/hotspot_cluster.py
─────────────────────────────────────────
RUNS: Every 24 hours (cron job)

INPUT:
├── karachi_crime.csv (CPLC data)
└── incidents/ from Firebase
        (crowdsourced reports)

ALGORITHM: DBSCAN
├── eps = 0.005        # ~500m radius
├── min_samples = 3    # min 3 incidents
└── metric = haversine

OUTPUT per cluster:
{
  center_lat: float,
  center_lng: float,
  radius_meters: int,
  incident_count: int,
  risk_level: "HIGH"|"MEDIUM",
  peak_hours: [20, 21, 22, 23],
  incident_types: ["mugging", "snatching"],
  trending: "up"|"stable"|"down"   ← NEW
}

STORED IN: Firebase hotspots/
```

FLOW 11 — Safe Route Recommender

```
FILE: ml/route_ranker.py
─────────────────────────────────────────
ENDPOINT: POST /route/recommend

STEP 1 — Fetch routes from Google Maps
└── alternatives=true → 2-3 routes

STEP 2 — Score each route
For each polyline point check:
├── Distance to nearest hotspot zone
├── Distance to high-risk signal     ← NEW
├── Time of day vs peak hours
└── Sum all penalties

STEP 3 — Return ranked routes:
{
  routes: [

      rank: 1,
      safety_label: "Safest Route",
      duration_minutes: 28,
      safety_score: 0.91,
      signals_on_route: 0,           ← NEW
      hotspots_on_route: 1,
      note: "3 mins longer but avoids
             Teen Talwar Signal and
             Baloch Colony underpass"
    },
    {
      rank: 2,
      safety_label: "Fastest Route",
      duration_minutes: 25,
      safety_score: 0.61,
      signals_on_route: 2,           ← NEW
      hotspots_on_route: 3,
      note: "Passes 2 high-risk signals.
             Not recommended after 9PM."
    }
  ]
}
```

from typing import Optional, List

    user_id: str
    origin_lat: float
    origin_lng: float
    destination_lat: float
    destination_lng: float
    contact_phone: str
    contact_name: str
    risk_level: str
    journey_type: str  # ride_hailing | solo | biker
    plate_number: Optional[str] = None

    journey_id: str
    current_lat: float
    current_lng: float
    current_speed: float
    timestamp: str


@router.post("/start")
def start_journey(req: JourneyStartRequest):
    journey_id = str(uuid.uuid4())

    # Get route polyline from Google Maps
    polyline, duration_seconds = get_route_polyline(
        req.origin_lat, req.origin_lng,
        req.destination_lat, req.destination_lng
    )

    # Pre-load signals on route (biker feature)
    signals_on_route = []
    if req.journey_type == "biker":
        signals_on_route = get_signals_on_route(polyline)

    # Sensitivity thresholds by risk level
    thresholds = {
        "LOW":    {"deviation_m": 500, "stop_min": 7,  "signal_warn_m": 200},
        "MEDIUM": {"deviation_m": 300, "stop_min": 5,  "signal_warn_m": 250},
        "HIGH":   {"deviation_m": 200, "stop_min": 3,  "signal_warn_m": 300},
    }
    t = thresholds.get(req.risk_level, thresholds["MEDIUM"])

    expected_arrival = (datetime.utcnow() + timedelta(seconds=duration_seconds)).strftime("%H:%M")

    journey_doc = {
        "userId": req.user_id,
        "status": "active",
        "journey_type": req.journey_type,
        "origin": {"lat": req.origin_lat, "lng": req.origin_lng},
        "destination": {"lat": req.destination_lat, "lng": req.destination_lng},
        "polyline": polyline,
        "risk_level": req.risk_level,
        "signals_on_route": signals_on_route,
        "warned_signals": [],
        "contact": {"name": req.contact_name, "phone": req.contact_phone},
        "consecutive_flags": 0,
        "last_lat": req.origin_lat,
        "last_lng": req.origin_lng,
        "last_ping": datetime.utcnow().isoformat(),
        "started_at": datetime.utcnow().isoformat(),
        "ended_at": None,
        "deviation_threshold_m": t["deviation_m"],
        "stop_threshold_min": t["stop_min"],
        "signal_warn_distance_m": t["signal_warn_m"],
    }

    db.collection("journeys").document(journey_id).set(journey_doc)

    return {
        "journey_id": journey_id,
        "polyline": polyline,
        "expected_arrival": expected_arrival,
        "timer_duration_seconds": duration_seconds + 600,  # 10 min buffer
        "deviation_threshold_meters": t["deviation_m"],
        "stop_threshold_minutes": t["stop_min"],
        "signals_on_route": signals_on_route,
    }


@router.post("/ping")
def ping_journey(req: JourneyPingRequest):
    journey_ref = db.collection("journeys").document(req.journey_id)
    journey = journey_ref.get().to_dict()

    if not journey or journey["status"] != "active":
        return {"status": "ok", "message": "Journey not active"}

    polyline = journey["polyline"]
    deviation_threshold = journey["deviation_threshold_m"]
    stop_threshold = journey["stop_threshold_min"]
    journey_type = journey["journey_type"]
    signals_on_route = journey.get("signals_on_route", [])
    warned_signals = journey.get("warned_signals", [])
    signal_warn_distance = journey.get("signal_warn_distance_m", 200)

    # Step 1: Check route deviation
    is_deviated = check_deviation(req.current_lat, req.current_lng, polyline, deviation_threshold)

    flags = journey.get("consecutive_flags", 0)
    if is_deviated:
        flags += 1
        journey_ref.update({"consecutive_flags": flags})
        if flags >= 3:
            return {"status": "alert", "message": "Route deviation detected"}
        return {"status": "deviation", "message": "You appear to be off your planned route"}

    # Reset flags if back on route
    if flags > 0:
        journey_ref.update({"consecutive_flags": 0})

    # Step 2: Check unusual stop
    stop_status = check_stop(req.current_lat, req.current_lng, req.current_speed, stop_threshold)
    if stop_status == "unusual_stop":
        return {"status": "stop", "message": "You appear to have stopped. Are you okay?"}

    # Step 3: Signal proximity check (biker only)
    if journey_type == "biker":
        from ml.signal_risk import check_signal_proximity
        signal_warning = check_signal_proximity(
            req.current_lat, req.current_lng,
            signals_on_route, warned_signals, signal_warn_distance
        )
        if signal_warning:
            # Mark signal as warned
            warned_signals.append(signal_warning["signal_id"])
            journey_ref.update({"warned_signals": warned_signals})
            return {
                "status": "signal_warning",
                "message": f"High-risk signal ahead: {signal_warning['name']}",
                "signal_data": signal_warning,
            }

    # Update last known position
    journey_ref.update({
        "last_lat": req.current_lat,
        "last_lng": req.current_lng,
        "last_ping": datetime.utcnow().isoformat(),
    })

    return {"status": "ok", "message": "All clear"}


@router.post("/end")
def end_journey(journey_id: str):
    db.collection("journeys").document(journey_id).update({
        "status": "completed",
        "ended_at": datetime.utcnow().isoformat(),
    })
    return {"status": "completed"}

from fastapi import APIRouter
from pydantic import BaseModel

import uuid

from services.firebase_service import db
from services.twilio_service import send_voice_call, send_sms
from services.maps_service import build_maps_link

router = APIRouter()


class AlertTriggerRequest(BaseModel):
    journey_id: str
    trigger_type: str  # timer_expired | route_deviation | unusual_stop | manual_sos
    current_lat: float
    current_lng: float


@router.post("/trigger")
def trigger_alert(req: AlertTriggerRequest):
    journey = db.collection("journeys").document(req.journey_id).get().to_dict()
    if not journey:
        return {"status": "error", "message": "Journey not found"}

    user = db.collection("users").document(journey["userId"]).get().to_dict()
    if not user:
        return {"status": "error", "message": "User not found"}

    name = user["name"]
    contact = journey["contact"]
    maps_link = build_maps_link(req.current_lat, req.current_lng)

    voice_message = (
        f"{name} was travelling and has not reached their destination. "
        f"Their last known location is being sent to you now."
    )

    sms_message = (
        f"{name} may need help.\n"
        f"Last known location:\n{maps_link}\n\n"
        f"Do NOT call them back — it may escalate the situation.\n"
        f"Go to location or contact authorities: 15 (Police)"
    )

    contacts = user.get("contacts", [])
    if contact.get("phone"):
        contacts.insert(0, contact)  # Trip contact first

    # Escalating voice calls — only for demo; real impl uses Twilio status callbacks
    contacted = []
    for c in contacts[:3]:
        send_voice_call(c["phone"], voice_message)
        send_sms(c["phone"], sms_message)
        contacted.append(c["phone"])

    alert_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
    db.collection("alerts").document(alert_id).set({
        "journeyId": req.journey_id,
        "trigger_type": req.trigger_type,
        "lat": req.current_lat,
        "lng": req.current_lng,
        "contacts_notified": contacted,
        "triggered_at": datetime.utcnow().isoformat(),
    })

"""
Detects when a user deviates from their planned route polyline.
Uses Shapely for point-to-linestring distance.
"""
from shapely.geometry import Point, LineString


def check_deviation(
    current_lat: float,
    current_lng: float,
    polyline: list,           # [[lat, lng], ...]
    threshold_meters: float = 300
) -> bool:
    """Returns True if user is more than threshold_meters from route."""
    if not polyline or len(polyline) < 2:
        return False

    # Shapely uses (lng, lat) — note coordinate order
    point = Point(current_lng, current_lat)
    line = LineString([(p[1], p[0]) for p in polyline])

    # Degrees to meters: 1 degree ≈ 111,139 meters at equator
    distance_deg = point.distance(line)
    distance_meters = distance_deg * 111_139

    return distance_meters > threshold_meters

Uses Shapely for point-to-linestring distance.
"""
from shapely.geometry import Point, LineString


def check_deviation(
    current_lat: float,
    current_lng: float,
    polyline: list,           # [[lat, lng], ...]
    threshold_meters: float = 300
) -> bool:
    """Returns True if user is more than threshold_meters from route."""
    if not polyline or len(polyline) < 2:
        return False

    # Shapely uses (lng, lat) — note coordinate order
    point = Point(current_lng, current_lat)
    line = LineString([(p[1], p[0]) for p in polyline])

    # Degrees to meters: 1 degree ≈ 111,139 meters at equator
    distance_deg = point.distance(line)
    distance_meters = distance_deg * 111_139

    return distance_meters > threshold_meters

        rows.append({

            "lng": d.get("lng"),
            "datetime": d.get("datetime"),
            "type": d.get("type"),
        })
    return pd.DataFrame(rows).dropna(subset=["lat", "lng"])

        counts = hours.value_counts()

    except Exception:
        return [20, 21, 22, 23]

    try:

        if doc.exists:
            prev = doc.to_dict().get("incident_count", current_count)
            if current_count > prev * 1.1:
                return "up"
            elif current_count < prev * 0.9:
                return "down"
    except Exception:

        db.collection("hotspots").document(hid).set(data)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    run_clustering()

from datetime import datetime
from geopy.distance import geodesic

def compute_signal_risk_score(signal_data: dict) -> tuple:
    """
    Returns (risk_score: float, risk_level: str)
    Formula:
        base_score = incidents_7d * 0.4 + incidents_30d * 0.2 + is_known_hotspot * 0.4
        time_multiplier = 1.5 if current hour in peak_hours else 0.5
        final = base_score * time_multiplier (clamped 0-1)
    """
    incidents_7d = signal_data.get("incident_count_week", 0)
    incidents_30d = signal_data.get("incident_count_month", 0)
    is_hotspot = 1 if signal_data.get("risk_level") == "HIGH" else 0

    base_score = (
        min(incidents_7d / 10.0, 1.0) * 0.4 +
        min(incidents_30d / 40.0, 1.0) * 0.2 +
        is_hotspot * 0.4
    )

    current_hour = datetime.utcnow().hour + 5  # PKT offset (UTC+5)
    current_hour = current_hour % 24
    peak_hours = signal_data.get("peak_hours", [])
    time_multiplier = 1.5 if current_hour in peak_hours else 0.5

    final_score = min(base_score * time_multiplier, 1.0)

    if final_score >= 0.7:
        level = "HIGH"
    elif final_score >= 0.4:
        level = "MEDIUM"
    else:
        level = "LOW"

    return round(final_score, 4), level

    polyline = [[lat, lng], ...]

        signal = signal_doc.to_dict()
        s_lat, s_lng = signal["lat"], signal["lng"]

        min_dist = float("inf")
        for point in polyline:
            d = geodesic((point[0], point[1]), (s_lat, s_lng)).meters
            if d < min_dist:
                min_dist = d

        if min_dist <= threshold_m:
            score, level = compute_signal_risk_score(signal)
            result.append({
                "signal_id": signal_doc.id,
                "name": signal.get("name", "Unknown Signal"),
                "lat": s_lat,
                "lng": s_lng,
                "distance_from_route_m": round(min_dist),
                "risk_level": level,
                "risk_score": score,
                "incident_count_week": signal.get("incident_count_week", 0),
                "peak_hours": signal.get("peak_hours", []),
            })

    result.sort(key=lambda x: x["risk_score"], reverse=True)
    return result

    current_lat: float,
    current_lng: float,
    signals_on_route: List[Dict],
    warned_signals: List[str],
    warn_distance_m: float = 200,
) -> Optional[Dict]:

    Returns signal data dict if warning should fire, else None.
    Only fires during peak hours.

    current_hour = (datetime.utcnow().hour + 5) % 24  # PKT

    for signal in signals_on_route:

        if dist <= warn_distance_m:
            if current_hour in signal.get("peak_hours", []):
                return {
                    **signal,
                    "distance_meters": round(dist),
                }

    return None

Route safety ranker — scores Google Maps alternatives by crime + signal risk.
"""
from geopy.distance import geodesic
from services.firebase_service import db
from ml.signal_risk import compute_signal_risk_score


def _get_hotspots():
    return [h.to_dict() for h in db.collection("hotspots").stream()]


def _get_signals():
    return [(s.id, s.to_dict()) for s in db.collection("signals").stream()]


def _route_penalty(polyline: list, hotspots: list, signals: list) -> dict:
    """Score a route. Lower = safer."""
    hotspot_penalty = 0
    signal_penalty = 0
    signals_on_route = 0
    hotspots_on_route = 0

    for point in polyline:
        lat, lng = point[0], point[1]

        for hs in hotspots:
            dist = geodesic((lat, lng), (hs["center_lat"], hs["center_lng"])).meters
            if dist < hs.get("radius_meters", 500):
                hotspot_penalty += 1
                hotspots_on_route += 1
                break

        for sid, sig in signals:
            dist = geodesic((lat, lng), (sig["lat"], sig["lng"])).meters
            if dist < 150:
                score, level = compute_signal_risk_score(sig)
                if level == "HIGH":
                    signal_penalty += score
                    signals_on_route += 1
                break

    return {
        "total_penalty": hotspot_penalty + signal_penalty * 2,
        "signals_on_route": signals_on_route,
        "hotspots_on_route": hotspots_on_route,
    }


def rank_routes(routes_from_maps: list) -> list:
    """
    routes_from_maps: list of dicts from Google Maps Directions API
    Each must have: polyline (list of [lat,lng]), duration_minutes
    Returns ranked list with safety info.
    """
    hotspots = _get_hotspots()
    signals = _get_signals()

    scored = []
    for route in routes_from_maps:
        polyline = route["polyline"]
        penalties = _route_penalty(polyline, hotspots, signals)
        total = penalties["total_penalty"]
        max_possible = len(polyline) * 3  # rough normalisation
        safety_score = round(1.0 - min(total / max(max_possible, 1), 1.0), 2)

        scored.append({
            **route,
            "safety_score": safety_score,
            "signals_on_route": penalties["signals_on_route"],
            "hotspots_on_route": penalties["hotspots_on_route"],
        })

    scored.sort(key=lambda x: x["safety_score"], reverse=True)

    labels = ["Safest Route", "Balanced Route", "Fastest Route"]
    for i, route in enumerate(scored):
        route["rank"] = i + 1
        route["safety_label"] = labels[i] if i < len(labels) else f"Route {i+1}"

    return scored

        "alternatives": str(alternatives).lower(),
        "key": MAPS_API_KEY,
    }
    resp = httpx.get(DIRECTIONS_URL, params=params, timeout=10)
    data = resp.json()

    if data.get("status") != "OK" or not data.get("routes"):

        return [[origin_lat, origin_lng], [dest_lat, dest_lng]], 1800

    route = data["routes"][0]["legs"][0]
    duration = route["duration"]["value"]

    # Decode overview polyline
    encoded = data["routes"][0]["overview_polyline"]["points"]

    points = []

                break
        dlng = ~(result >> 1) if result & 1 else result >> 1
        lng += dlng

        points.append([lat / 1e5, lng / 1e5])
    return points


def build_maps_link(lat: float, lng: float) -> str:
    return f"https://maps.google.com/?q={lat},{lng}"

# Bachao Pakistan — What You Need To Do

All 57 files are written. Here is exactly what you need to do to get this running.

---

## STEP 1 — Get Your API Keys (do this first, everything depends on it)

### Firebase
1. Go to https://console.firebase.google.com → Create a new project → call it `bachao-pakistan`
2. Enable **Firestore Database** (start in test mode)
3. Enable **Authentication** → Phone
4. Go to Project Settings → Service Accounts → Generate new private key → download JSON
5. From that JSON, copy `project_id`, `private_key`, `client_email`
6. Go to Project Settings → General → Your apps → Add a Web app → copy the `firebaseConfig` object

### Google Maps
1. Go to https://console.cloud.google.com → Create a project
2. Enable these APIs: **Maps JavaScript API**, **Directions API**, **Places API**, **Geocoding API**
3. Create an API key → copy it

### Twilio
1. Go to https://console.twilio.com → Create an account
2. Get a phone number (free trial gives you one)
3. Copy Account SID, Auth Token, and your Twilio phone number

---

## STEP 2 — Backend Setup

```bash
cd bachao-pakistan/backend

# Copy and fill in your keys
cp .env.example .env
# Open .env and fill in every value

# Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

# Run locally
python main.py
# → API now running at http://localhost:8000
# → Visit http://localhost:8000/docs to see all endpoints
```

**One thing you must do manually in backend:** The risk scorer uses simulated training data. Before production, replace the `CRIME_INDEX` dict in `ml/risk_scorer.py` with real values from your `karachi_crime.csv`. The file goes in `backend/data/karachi_crime.csv` — expected columns: `lat`, `lng`, `datetime`, `type`.

**Also:** `ml/stop_detector.py` has a few hardcoded traffic zones. Add more from `data/traffic_hotspots.geojson` when you have it.

---

## STEP 3 — Seed the Signals Database

The signals collection in Firebase needs to be populated. You have two options:

**Option A (quick demo):** Manually add 5–10 signals in Firebase Console → Firestore → signals collection. Each document needs:
```json
{
  "name": "Teen Talwar Signal",
  "lat": 24.8234,
  "lng": 67.0123,
  "area": "Clifton",
  "risk_level": "HIGH",
  "incident_count_week": 4,
  "incident_count_month": 11,
  "peak_hours": [21, 22, 23],
  "incident_types": ["phone_snatching"],
  "last_updated": "2024-11-15T00:00:00"
}
```

**Option B (proper):** Import from `data/karachi_signals.geojson` using a migration script (you write this once — just read the geojson and write each feature as a Firestore document).

---

## STEP 4 — Run the First Hotspot Clustering

```bash
cd bachao-pakistan/backend
python -m ml.hotspot_cluster
```

This reads your crime CSV + Firebase incidents, runs DBSCAN, and writes hotspot zones to Firestore. Set this up as a cron job (Railway supports this, or use a simple Python schedule).

---

## STEP 5 — Mobile App Setup

```bash
cd bachao-pakistan/mobile

npm install

# Open src/utils/firebase.js
# Replace all "YOUR_..." placeholders with your Firebase web app config

# Open src/utils/constants.js
# Change API_BASE_URL to http://localhost:8000 for local dev
# or to your Railway URL for production

# Run on your phone
npx expo start
# Scan QR with Expo Go app
```

**Two things you must wire up in the mobile app:**

1. **Google Places Autocomplete** in `JourneySetup.jsx` — there's a `// TODO` comment where you need to add destination geocoding. Install `expo-google-places-autocomplete` or use Google's REST Geocoding API via `maps_service` on the backend.

2. **Firebase Phone Auth** — in `Onboarding.jsx`, `signInWithPhoneNumber` requires your Firebase app to have Phone Auth enabled with a verified domain or test phone numbers. For the demo, add your test phone number in Firebase Console → Authentication → Sign-in method → Phone → Phone numbers for testing.

---

## STEP 6 — Web App Setup

```bash
cd bachao-pakistan/web

npm install

# Copy and fill in your keys
cp .env.example .env
# Fill in VITE_GOOGLE_MAPS_KEY and all VITE_FIREBASE_* values

# Run locally
npm run dev
# → http://localhost:5173

# Deploy to Vercel
npx vercel
# Add the same env vars in Vercel dashboard → Settings → Environment Variables
```

---

## STEP 7 — Deploy Backend to Railway

1. Go to https://railway.app → New project → Deploy from GitHub repo
2. Set root directory to `backend/`
3. Add all your env vars from `.env` in Railway → Variables tab
4. Railway auto-detects Python and runs `uvicorn main:app`
5. Copy the generated URL → update `API_BASE_URL` in mobile `constants.js` and `VITE_API_URL` in web `.env`

---

- All API endpoints wired and connected
- ML risk scorer (trains on simulated data at startup — works immediately)
- Route deviation detection (Shapely geometry — works immediately)
- Stop detection logic
- Signal proximity detection for biker mode
- DBSCAN clustering logic
- Twilio voice call + SMS pipeline
- Google polyline decoder
- All mobile screens with full navigation
- Shake detector (3 shakes → SOS)
- GPS poller (pings backend every 30s)
- Signal warning component (vibrate + banner, no sound)
- Full web app with dark map, signal pins, filters
- Firebase schema matching the spec exactly

---

- [ ] Backend running (Railway or localhost)
- [ ] At least 5–10 signals seeded in Firebase with realistic data
- [ ] At least 2–3 hotspots (run clustering after adding a few incidents manually)
- [ ] Mobile app on Expo Go, phone auth working with test numbers
- [ ] Web app deployed on Vercel with your Google Maps key

---

## Known Gaps to Fix Before Production (not needed for demo)

- Google Places autocomplete in JourneySetup (currently uses hardcoded coords)
- Real `karachi_crime.csv` data from CPLC
- `karachi_signals.geojson` with all Karachi signals
- Background location on iOS (requires physical device + EAS build, not Expo Go)
- Twilio escalation logic (currently calls all contacts simultaneously — add status callbacks for sequential escalation)
- Firebase security rules (currently in test mode — lock down before launch)
